provenance.base: instruction.md 6.2: built from the FICO HELOC data dictionary, as instructed
provenance.reason: The HELOC SCM has no literal specification in the instruction; the structure below follows the bureau-file arithmetic described in the FICO data dictionary.

notes: ExternalRiskEstimate is a consolidated bureau score computed *from* the other variables, so it is a child of them and can never be an intervention target. Methods that propose 'raise your risk score by 10 points' are proposing a change to an output, which is exactly the failure mode this project measures.

The three deterministic aggregates are the causal-validity test cases: PercentTradesNeverDelq is a function of NumSatisfactoryTrades/NumTotalTrades and MaxDelqEver, PercentTradesWBalance of NumRevolvingTradesWBalance/NumTotalTrades, and AverageMInFile of MSinceOldestTradeOpen and NumTradesOpeninLast12M.

Opening an account is a single act with three simultaneous consequences (NumTotalTrades up, NumTradesOpeninLast12M up, AverageMInFile down); a method that reports only one of them understates the true cost of its own advice.
MSinceOldestTradeOpen can only be increased by waiting, hence very_high rather than infinite: it is reachable, just not this month.
HELOC ships no demographic columns, so the sensitive set is genuinely empty; the fairness analysis for this dataset is therefore reported as not applicable rather than as passing.
